title: टि. एस. एलियटका मूलभूत साहित्य सिद्धान्तहरू
nepali: टमस स्टर्न एलियटका ‘परम्परा र व्यक्तिप्रतिभा (Tradition and the Individual Talent) को सिद्धान्त, निर्वैयक्तिकताको सिद्धान्त (Impersonal theory of poetry), वस्तुगत समीकरण (Objective corelative) को सिद्धान्त र समन्वित संवेदना (unified sensibility) को सिद्धान्त’ जस्ता साहित्य सिद्धान्तलाई सङ्क्षिप्त एवं प्रस्टरूपमा प्रस्तुत गर्ने उद्देश्यमा केन्द्रित यस लेखका लागि पुस्तकालयीय स्रोतबाट सामग्री सङ्कलन गरिएको छ र यसरी सङ्कलित सामग्रीको विश्लेषण गरेर सिद्धान्तको परीक्षण गरिएको छ । लेखमा सर्वप्रथम इलियटको सङ्क्षिप्त परिचय दिनुका साथै उनका सिद्धान्तहरूको पृष्ठभूमि प्रस्तुत गरिएको छ र अन्त्यमा परम्परालाई त्रिकालिकता प्रदान गरेर हरेक कालखण्डमा आउने व्यक्तिप्रतिभालाई अखण्ड परम्परामा सामेल गराउँदै परम्पराकै सापेक्षतामा व्यक्तिप्रतिभाको मूल्याङ्कन गरी उसका स्थानको निर्धारण–पुनर्निर्धारण गरिन्छ भन्ने सिद्धान्त नै परम्परा र व्यक्तिप्रतिभाको सिद्धान्त हो । प्रतिभाशाली कलाकारले आफ्ना अनुभूति, भावना र संवेदनालाई नवीनतासाथ निर्वैयक्तिक रूपमा प्रस्तुत गरेमा सिर्जना उत्कृष्ट बन्दछ । साहित्यकारले आपूmले प्रकट गर्न चाहेका रागात्मक आवेग, अनुभूति, भाव वा विचारलाई वस्तुगतता र नाटकीयता दिएर समानार्थ–अभिव्यञ्जक संवेग वा वस्तु–संघटना, स्थिति वा घटना–शृङ्खलाजस्ता बाह्य वस्तुहरूद्वारा अभिव्यञ्जित गर्नुपर्छ भन्ने एलियटको वस्तुगत समीकरणको सिद्धान्तलाई पौरस्य काव्य चिन्तनअन्तर्गत रससिद्धान्तका कोणबाट हेर्दा ‘भाव अनुकूलका विभाव, अनुभाव र व्यभिचारी भावको प्रयोग वा विभावादि–विधान’ का रूपमा पनि बुझ्न सकिने देखिन्छ । चिन्तन अनुभूतिमय र अनुभूति चिन्तनमय बन्न सक्नु नै एलियटले चाहेको आदर्श स्थिति हो र यही नै उनको समन्वित संवेदनाको सिद्धान्तको मर्म हो भन्ने निष्कर्ष निकालिएको छ ।
american_english: Focused on the objective of presenting concisely and clearly literary theories such as T. S. Eliot's theory of 'Tradition and the Individual Talent', the theory of impersonality, the theory of objective correlative, and the theory of unified sensibility, material has been collected from library sources for this article, and the theory has been tested by analyzing the material thus collected. In the article, first a brief introduction of Eliot is given along with the background of his theories, and finally the theory that is 'Tradition and the Individual Talent' is the one which, by giving tri-temporality to tradition, incorporates the individual talent coming in every period into the unbroken tradition and evaluates the individual talent relative to tradition, thereby determining–redetermining his place. If a talented artist presents his feelings, emotions and sensibilities in a novel way impersonally, the creation becomes excellent. When Eliot's theory of objective correlative — that the emotional urge, feeling, sentiment or thought the writer wishes to express must be expressed through external objects such as an analogous-expressive emotion or object-configuration, situation or chain of events, giving them objectivity and dramatic quality — is viewed from the angle of rasa theory under ancient poetic thought, it can also be understood in the form of 'the use of vibhava, anubhava and vyabhicari bhava suited to the sentiment, or the vibhavadi-vidhana'. The conclusion drawn is that thought becoming feeling and feeling becoming thought being possible is the ideal state Eliot desired, and this is the essence of his theory of unified sensibility.

informal_english: Focused on giving a short, clear rundown of literary theories like T. S. Eliot's 'Tradition and the Individual Talent', the impersonal theory of poetry, the objective correlative and unified sensibility, this article pulls material from library sources and tests the theories by analysing what's collected. The article first gives a quick intro to Eliot and the background of his theories, and finishes up with the idea that 'Tradition and the Individual Talent' is the theory where, by giving tradition a three-timed permanence, each period's individual talent gets folded into the unbroken tradition and judged relative to tradition, working out and re-working out that person's place. If a talented artist presents their feelings, emotions and sensibilities in a fresh, impersonal way, the work turns out excellent. When you look at Eliot's objective correlative — that the emotional urge, feeling, sentiment or thought the writer wants to express has to be expressed through external objects like an analogous-expressive emotion or object-configuration, situation or chain of events, giving them objectivity and dramatic quality — from the angle of rasa theory under ancient poetic thought, you can also read it as 'the use of vibhava, anubhava and vyabhicari bhava suited to the sentiment, or the vibhavadi-vidhana'. The wrap-up conclusion is that thought turning into feeling and feeling turning into thought being possible is the ideal state Eliot wanted, and that's the heart of his theory of unified sensibility.
